findings.description: Preexisting node_modules/next 16.2.7 contradicted both declared and locked Next 16.3.1.
findings.repair: Rebuilt node_modules with npm ci from exact frozen package.json/package-lock.json bytes, then replaced installed tree.

findings.description: Passing fresh packet-level capture metadata to a whole historical payload would label earlier rows R0.
findings.evidence: Regression tests distinguish current selected row R0 and older retained rows R2.
findings.repair: Per-row closed-session eligibility, upstream R2 preservation and weakest-parent aggregation in new source boundary.

findings.description: Frozen assembler's fallback observation end is date-only UTC day-end; a source with evidenced earlier settlement close would remain unavailable before day-end unless parent end is propagated.
findings.evidence: Complete synthetic R0 pipeline test initially showed only VX_NEAR_CONTRACTS_UNAVAILABLE, then passed after explicit max-near-parent observation end propagation.
findings.repair: New loader propagates the latest near-parent evidenced end using the source-specific calendar. No assembler/core/oracle modification.

findings.description: Repeated observations of one unchanged session could reset accumulated diagnostic ages and candidate counts.
findings.repair: Preserve the checkpoint for SAME_SESSION_REOBSERVED without double counting; censor actual revisions, gaps, failures and version changes.

findings.description: A blocked private source read could retain the public V1 request indefinitely.
findings.repair: Bound asynchronous sidecar waiting to 2000 ms and active sidecars/publications to eight; retain V1 result/error identity and emit timeout diagnostics. This is not a freshness TTL and cannot interrupt synchronous JavaScript.

findings.description: A mutable active bundle alone would lose the exact source envelope used by an earlier snapshot.
findings.repair: Archive exact original bundle bytes outside Git under their SHA before parsing; reject corruption and preserve every vintage reference.

findings.description: The complete 33,474-row raw bundle recreated Intl date formatters per Yahoo row and repeated normalization for every changed asOf; the initial benchmark observed approximately 560 ms per cut and 1.21 GB RSS.
findings.repair: Reuse an identical per-call date formatter and one immutable normalized vintage keyed by bytes/contracts. Resolve calendars, VX and a distinct normalized input again for every asOf; evaluate unchanged C03. Verify the mechanical normalizer inverse and full original-output equality.

operationalLimitations: Default OFF. No deployment configuration, scheduler, Designer or production cutover was enabled.

Five real CFE response captures prove local acquisition/retention and honest INCOMPLETE/UNKNOWN degradation. No real official calendar or complete prospective source bundle was configured; complete R0 replay tests are synthetic.
The local smoke archive is temporary, not a configured durable deployment store. Runtime requires private storage with a single writer and an operator retention policy.
Capture-time bounds do not prove provider publication. R2 history stays R2; no R1 certification or PIT OOS claim.

Performance measurements use controlled unavailable V1 providers and preserved full R2 source bytes on this host. They exclude live provider latency, rendering and deployment load; no SLA is invented.
The sidecar wait deadline cannot preempt synchronous code, and a process shutdown can interrupt outstanding I/O. Logs may be the only evidence when storage itself fails.
The 100/100/60 event counts and both STRESS branches require future governed evidence/adjudication. Diagnostic counts do not change C03 or authorize automatic promotion.
